capabilities: render table, board, gallery, list, calendar, timeline and chart views over a folder of notes
edit rows inline with 18 typed frontmatter columns including select, status, date and media
compute formula, relation, lookup and rollup columns across linked databases
filter, sort, aggregate and bulk-edit rows, with CSV import and export
embed any database view in notes and auto-arrange rows into subfolders by property values
disambiguation: Not a Notion integration; all data stays as local Markdown files and the plugin never connects to Notion.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.8.7 or later; supports desktop and mobile. UI is translated into 7 languages (en, pt-BR, es, fr, de, zh, ja).
intentEvidence: Notion Bases focuses on a different set of trade-offs — more views, more column types, and a spreadsheet-style formula syntax.
motivation: The author wanted Notion-level databases inside Obsidian: "If you ever wished Obsidian had Notion-level databases without leaving your vault, this is it."
problem: Obsidian's built-in Bases plugin only covers tables and list views with limited column types and an expression-based formula system, lacking Notion-style database views and modeling.

relations.evidence: Obsidian's built-in Bases plugin is great for tables and has its own expression-based formula system.
Turn any folder into a Notion-style database with Table, Board (Kanban), Gallery, List, Calendar, Timeline (Gantt), and Chart views

summary: Database engine that turns any folder of Markdown notes into table, kanban, gallery, list, calendar, timeline and chart views driven by frontmatter.
